sections.html:
Deeds for the county go to 12265 M-32 West in Atlanta, mailing box 789, ZIP 49709. Phone 989-785-8079. The posted window is Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the counter stays staffed at midday.

The register is the recording officer for anything that transfers or burdens land here, including mineral interests along with surface interests. Each paper gets an exact receipt time, a liber and page, and a line in the entry book. Originals are scanned and sent to microfiche for off-site archive storage, and a tract index lets a searcher start from the legal description rather than a name.

The same staff chair the county plat board and take passport applications. Abstractors, title companies, mortgage lenders, oil and gas land agents and township assessors all rely on this counter.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Montmorency County
sections.html:
Montmorency sits in Northern Michigan, and most of its 547 square miles of land is state forest with lakes left by glaciers. Atlanta, the county seat, is an unincorporated community 46 miles west of Alpena and 32 miles east of Gaylord. Hillman, a village, lies 15 miles east-northeast.

Only 9,153 people lived here in 2020, and the estimate for July 2025 is 9,842. The 2020 census counted 8,930 housing units with 51.6% of them vacant, a share that goes with a market of cabins, lake lots and trail traffic. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $158,600.

If your parcel is rural, confirm which township it sits in, since the local unit handles assessing and your title company will need it. Townships are Albert, Avery, Briley, Hillman, Loud, Montmorency, Rust and Vienna, plus the Village of Hillman.

Trail access drives much of the local market. The county's ORV, ATV and snowmobile trails are among the best in the state, and it is one of the few counties that let ATVs ride public county roads, which links fuel stops, food and lodging in Hillman, Atlanta and Lewiston. Buyers who hunt, fish or ride often care more about where a parcel touches state forest or a lake than about square footage.

A house near the Thunder Bay River or a lake lot can read as a rental or a weekend place to a buyer. State the road type, the water frontage and any recorded easement in the listing, then confirm each against the register's index before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Forms and helpers on the county page
sections.html:
The county page carries downloads for a quit claim deed, a warranty deed, an affidavit of affixture for a mobile home, a notice of intention to maintain mineral rights and a principal residence exemption form. It also posts fee sheets for statutory charges, copies and searches, commercial code filings, recording standards and transfer tax, with separate sheets for county exemptions, state exemptions and valuation.

For a cabin, hunting parcel or acreage, three items come up most.

  • A deed that repeats the legal description exactly, because the tract index runs on it.
  • A recorded survey when a boundary matters. The page lists several surveyors and independent searchers in the region.
  • Mobile home or mineral paperwork, when either appears in the chain of title.

Title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord are also listed. One of them can draft the deed and order the search that a buyer will want, which the register's staff cannot do.

Michigan's judicature act sets $30.00 as the base recording charge. A county that is not chartered cannot go above the state schedule, so the sheet on the county site is the number to follow.

Montmorency County recording and search charges
ServiceCharge
Record a deed or similar paper$30.00
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged in one paper$3.00
Name search50 cents a year, $5.00 minimum

The county page also posts separate sheets for copies and for uniform commercial code filings. Phone 989-785-8079 if you plan to mail a check and want the total confirmed.

Ask the office about the format of any commercial filing before you send it.

The state takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 of price or part of it, and the county treasurer receives payment within 15 days. The seller owes it.

A deed for under $100, a land contract that keeps title with the seller until paid in full, and a corrective quitclaim all sit outside both taxes. For a parcel that crosses a county line, split the price and pay each county its share. Separate county and state exemption sheets on the county page show which others apply.

A sale resets taxable value. Under MCL 211.27a the next year's figure moves up to state equalized value, half of true cash value, and the buyer informs the local assessor within 45 days. A cabin held for decades can carry a taxable value far below that number, so the new owner may see a jump. A parent, child, sibling or grandchild who keeps a residence non-commercial is excepted, and so is a surviving spouse.

An inherited property counts as a transfer when it passes by will or intestacy to anyone outside those groups. Ask the township assessor which rule fits before you decide on a price, since the next owner's bill may differ a lot from yours. The Montmorency County treasurer can report the parcel's tax status before you set a closing date.

If the seller took the homestead exemption, it must be rescinded on Form 2602 within 90 days of the house ceasing to be the owner's home.

sections.h2: Getting a cabin or acreage ready to close
sections.html:
Order a title search early, since mineral interests and old easements can sit in the chain of title for a long time. If a mobile home is part of the sale, look for the affidavit of affixture. Have the deed prepared by a title company or attorney, then bring the original to the Atlanta counter with the $30.00 fee and the transfer tax paperwork. A cash buyer can often close faster, but the same search and recording steps apply.

Expect the buyer's title company to ask for the legal description, any recorded survey and the names on the earlier deed. If the property crosses a county line, tell the agent early, since the price must be split and tax paid to each county. Sellers who claimed the homestead exemption should rescind it, and anyone selling by land contract should ask whether the contract is exempt from transfer tax before recording anything.

faqs.q: Is the Montmorency County register of deeds open at lunchtime?
faqs.a: Yes. The office stays open during lunch hours, with a weekday window of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone is 989-785-8079.

faqs.q: How is transfer tax figured in Montmorency County?
faqs.a: The state takes $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500. The seller owes it, and it is paid to the county treasurer within 15 days.

faqs.q: Can the office prepare my quit claim deed?
faqs.a: No. It records and indexes. The county page offers quit claim and warranty deed forms, but a title company or attorney should confirm which one fits your transfer.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether mineral rights were severed?
faqs.a: Ask a title company to search the chain of title. The register records mineral interests apart from surface interests, and the county page lists a notice form for keeping mineral rights.

faqs.q: Where can I find Atlanta-area title companies?
faqs.a: The register of deeds page lists title companies in Atlanta, Alpena and Gaylord, as well as surveyors and independent searchers in the area.
